Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Treat the wagtails with goodness, meaning the swallows, for these are the friendliest of the birds of the people with the people'.
Then he (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'And do you know what the wagtail (swallow) says when it passes by and sings? It says: In the Name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful'.

ai.seo_question: What does the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) say about the recitation of swallows?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration to highlight the spiritual sensitivity of creation, where the swallow's song is interpreted as a literal recitation of Surah Al-Fatiha, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the ubiquity of divine praise in nature. The Prophet’s extension of his voice on 'wa lā al-dāllīn' underscores the significance of this phrase in liturgical practice and serves as a reminder of the bird's innate connection to human worship.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from sahl Bin Ziyad, and Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, altogether from Al Jamourany, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Bin Abu Hamza, from Muhammad Bin Yusuf Al Tameemy, 
(It has been narrated) from Muhammad son of Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, from his father<sup>asws</sup> who said, ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Treat the wagtails with goodness, meaning the swallows, for these are the friendliest of the birds of the people with the people’.
Then he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘And are you knowing what the wagtail (swallow) is saying when it passes by and sings? She is saying, ‘In the Name of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> the Beneficent, the Merciful.
The Praise is for Allahazwj Lordazwj of the Worlds’ – until hesaww recited the ‘Mother of the Book’ (Surah Al-Fatiha, Chapter 1).
So when it comes the end of its singing, so she says, ‘Wa La Zalleeen’ (last Words of Surah al-Fatiha).
Rasool-Allahsaww extended hissaww voice with it, ‘Wa La Zalleen’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ahmad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah all from al-Jamuraniy from al-Hassan ibn Ali ibn abu Hamzah from Muhammad ibn Yusuf al-Tamimiy from Muhammad ibn Ja‘far from his father who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, recommended to be good to al-Sininat (the crows). They among the birds are the ones that feel comfortable with people
and he (the Messenger of Allah) then said, ‘Do you know what al-Sininah says when it passes by or sings? It says, “In the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful,
All praise belongs to Allah, Cherisher of the worlds
. . .” until it reads ’Umm al-Kitab (the first chapter of al-Quran)
and in the end it sings, “Waladdallin”.
’ He (the Messenger of Allah) prolonged his voice saying, ‘waladdallin
